prompt_text:
Task: Federated Login Flow

Write code that implements a PKCE login flow for public clients using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Google Identity Platform OIDC:
  Service: Google Identity Platform
  SDK: REST / firebase-admin
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: signInWithIdp, OIDC provider config
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/web/oidc

Option 2 — Alibaba Cloud IDaaS EIAM OIDC:
  Service: IDaaS EIAM OIDC
  SDK: OIDC REST
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_IDAAS_ISSUER, ALIBABA_IDAAS_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/idaas/eiam/developer-reference/integrate-sso-with-oidc

Option 3 — IBM App ID Federation:
  Service: IBM Cloud App ID federation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: IBM_APPID_CLIENT_ID, IBM_APPID_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/appid?topic=appid-enterprise

Option 4 — Auth0:
  Service: Auth0 Authentication API
  SDK: auth0-python / OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, oauth/token, userinfo
  Setup hints: AUTH0_DOMAIN, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://auth0.com/docs/api/authentication

Option 5 — Cognito Hosted UI Federation:
  Service: Amazon Cognito federation
  SDK: boto3 + OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: COGNITO_DOMAIN, COGNITO_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-provider.html

Option 6 — Microsoft Entra OIDC:
  Service: Microsoft identity platform
  SDK: msal
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: get_authorization_request_url, acquire_token_by_authorization_code
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os import uuid import flask import msal import requests from flask import Flask, redirect, render_template_string, request, session, url_for # This application uses the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for Python # to implement the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. # You must have the following environment variables set: # AZURE_CLIENT_ID: The Application (client) ID of your Azure AD App Registration. # AZURE_TENANT_ID: The Directory (tenant) ID of your Azure AD App Registration. # The App Registration must be configured for a "Single-page application" or "Mobile and desktop applications" # platform with a Redirect URI matching the one used in this application (e.g., http://localhost:5000/getAToken). CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("AZURE_CLIENT_ID") TENANT_ID = os.getenv("AZURE_TENANT_ID") AUTHORITY = f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{TENANT_ID}" REDIRECT_PATH = "/getAToken" # The path portion of the redirect URI # These are the permissions the app requires. # For this example, we'll request the user's basic profile information. SCOPE = ["User.Read"] # This is the Microsoft Graph API endpoint for the current user's profile GRAPH_API_ENDPOINT = "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me" # Initialize Flask app app = Flask(__name__) # A secret key is required for Flask session management app.secret_key = os.urandom(24) def _build_msal_app(cache=None): """ Initializes a new MSAL PublicClientApplication instance. Public clients are apps that can't securely store secrets. """ return msal.PublicClientApplication( CLIENT_ID, authority=AUTHORITY, token_cache=cache ) def _get_token_from_cache(): """ Retrieves a token from the session cache if available. """ cache = msal.SerializableTokenCache() if session.get("token_cache"): cache.deserialize(session["token_cache"]) msal_app = _build_msal_app(cache) accounts = msal_app.get_accounts() if accounts: # Attempt to acquire a token silently from the cache result = msal_app.acquire_token_silent(SCOPE, account=accounts[0]) session["token_cache"] = cache.serialize() return result return None @app.route("/") def index(): """ Main page. Displays user info if logged in, otherwise a login link. """ token = _get_token_from_cache() user_claims = token.get("id_token_claims") if token else None return render_template_string("""

MSAL Python PKCE Demo

{% if user %}

Welcome, {{ user.get('name') }}!

You are authenticated.

Call Microsoft Graph API
Logout {% else %} Login {% endif %} """, user=user_claims) @app.route("/login") def login(): """ Initiates the PKCE authentication flow. MSAL handles the generation of the code verifier and challenge. """ # Create a flow object and store it in the session auth_code_flow = _build_msal_app().initiate_auth_code_flow( scopes=SCOPE, redirect_uri=url_for("authorized", _external=True, _scheme='http') ) session["flow"] = auth_code_flow # Redirect the user to the Azure AD authorization endpoint return redirect(auth_code_flow["auth_uri"]) @app.route(REDIRECT_PATH) def authorized(): """ Handles the redirect back from Azure AD. Exchanges the authorization code for an access token. """ try: cache = msal.SerializableTokenCache() # Use the flow from the session to complete the token acquisition result = _build_msal_app(cache=cache).acquire_token_by_auth_code_flow( session.get("flow", {}), request.args ) if "error" in result: return render_template_string("""

Login Failed

Error: {{ error }}

Description: {{ error_description }}

Home """, **result) # Store user info and token cache in the session session["user"] = result.get("id_token_claims") session["token_cache"] = cache.serialize() except ValueError as e: # Handle potential errors, e.g., state mismatch return f"Error acquiring token: {e}", 400 return redirect(url_for("index")) @app.route("/logout") def logout(): """ Logs the user out by clearing the session and redirecting to Azure AD logout. """ session.clear() logout_uri = ( f"{AUTHORITY}/oauth2/v2.0/logout" f"?post_logout_redirect_uri={url_for('index', _external=True)}" ) return redirect(logout_uri) @app.route("/graphcall") def graphcall(): """ Example of using the access token to call a protected API. """ token = _get_token_from_cache() if not token or "access_token" not in token: return redirect(url_for("login")) response = requests.get( GRAPH_API_ENDPOINT, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token['access_token']} ) # Check for a successful response if response.status_code == 200: return flask.jsonify(response.json()) else: return f"Error calling Graph API: {response.status_code} - {response.text}", 500 if __name__ == "__main__": # In a production environment, this should be run behind a proper WSGI server. # The redirect URI in Azure AD must match the one used here. # For local development, localhost with a port is typical. # Ensure FLASK_DEBUG is not used in production. app.run(port=5000, debug=True)
